    #Heat Transfer Mechanism

    Energy balance for a control volume:

    dtdEsys​​=E˙in​−E˙out​+E˙gen​

    E˙st​=Q˙​in​−Q˙​out​+E˙gen​

    E˙st​=Q˙​in​−Q˙​out​+e˙gen​V

    where V is volume of a medium

    Energy balance for a control surface:

    E˙in​=E˙out​

    Q˙​in​=Q˙​out​

    Since V=0 for a control surface, E˙st​=E˙gen​=0.

    #Fourier’s Law of Conduction

    Total heat transfer via conduction:

    Q˙​cond​=−kAdxdT​

    where k is thermal conductivity of a material (W/m⋅K),
    and     A is area normal to the direction of heat transfer

    Total heat flux:

    q˙​cond​=−kdxdT​

    #Newton’s Law of Cooling

    Total heat transfer via convection:

    Q˙​conv​=hAs​(Ts​−T∞​)

    where h is convection heat transfer coefficient (W/m2⋅K),
    and     As​ is the surface area in contact with the fluid

    Total heat flux:

    q˙​conv​=h(Ts​−T∞​)

    Note that the temperature difference follows the direction of heat transfer.
    If     Ts​>T∞​, the surface is losing heat to the environment, thus Ts​−T∞​.
    If     Ts​<T∞​, the surface is gaining heat from environment, thus T∞​−Ts​.

    #Radiation Heat Transfer

    Maximum rate of radiation emitted by a blackbody:

    Q˙​emit,max​=σAs​Ts​4

    where Boltzmann’s constant σ=5.67×10−8 W/m2⋅K4

    Rate of radiation emitted by a real surface:

    Q˙​emit​=εσAs​Ts​4

    where ε is emissivity of a surface, ranging from 0≤ε≤1, with ε=1 for a blackbody

    Incident radiation absorbed by a real surface:

    Q˙​absorb​=αQ˙​incident​=ασAs​Tsurr​4

    where absorptivity α ranges from 0≤α≤1, with α=1 for a blackbody

    Net radiation heat transfer:

    Q˙​rad​=Q˙​emit​−Q˙​absorb​

    Q˙​rad​=εσAs​Ts​4−ασAs​Tsurr​4

    Q˙​rad​=εσAs​(Ts​4−Tsurr​4)

    Surrounding surfaces are treated as blackbodies.
    Surface of interest is treated as a gray surface, such that     ε=α.

    Linearized radiation heat transfer coefficient:

    hrad​=εσ(Ts​2+Tsurr​2)(Ts​+Tsurr​)

    hrad​=εσ4Tm​4

    where mean temperature Tm​=2Ts​+Tsurr​​

    #Heat Conduction Equation

    Conduction equation in rectangular coordinates:

    ρc∂t∂T​=∂x∂​(k∂x∂T​)+∂y∂​(k∂y∂T​)+∂z∂​(k∂z∂T​)+e˙gen​

    where e˙gen​ is heat generation per unit volume (W/m3)

    If thermal conductivity k is a constant:

    α1​∂t∂T​=∂x2∂2T​+∂y2∂2T​+∂z2∂2T​+ke˙gen​​

    where α=ρck​ is thermal diffusivity of a material (m2/s)

    Conduction equation in cylindrical coordinates:

    ρc∂t∂T​=r1​∂r∂​(kr∂r∂T​)+r21​∂ϕ∂​(k∂ϕ∂T​)+∂z∂​(k∂z∂T​)+e˙gen​

    Conduction equation in spherical coordinates:

    ρc∂t∂T​=r21​∂r∂​(kr2∂r∂T​)+r2sin2θ1​∂ϕ∂​(k∂ϕ∂T​)+r2sinθ1​∂θ∂​(ksinθ∂θ∂T​)+e˙gen​

    #Boundary Conditions

    Constant Surface Temperature

    T(0,t)=T1​

    T(L,t)=T2​

    Constant Heat Flux

    Supply of heat into control volume:

    q˙​supply​=−k∂x∂T​​x=0​

    Insulated (adiabatic) surface:

    ∂x∂T​​x=0​=0

    Geometry/thermal symmetry:

    ∂x∂T​=0

    Convection Boundary Condition

    For 1D heat transfer in a plane wall:

    −k∂x∂T​​x=0​=h1​[T∞1​​−T(0,t)]

    −k∂x∂T​​x=L​=h2​[T(L,t)−T∞2​​]

    Radiation Boundary Condition

    For 1D heat transfer in a plane wall:

    −k∂x∂T​​x=0​=ε1​σ[Tsurr,1​4−T(0,t)4]

    −k∂x∂T​​x=L​=ε2​σ[T(L,t)4−Tsurr,2​4]

    Interface Boundary Condition

    Interface of two mediums in contact:

    TA​(x0​,t)=TB​(x0​,t)

    −kA​∂x∂TA​​​x=x0​​=−kB​∂x∂TB​​​x=x0​​

    #Heat Generation in a Solid

    Conduction in a Plane Wall

    Asymmetrical boundary condition:

    T(x)=2ke˙gen​​L2(1−L2x2​)+2LT2​−T1​​x+2T1​+T2​​

    Symmetrical boundary condition:

    T(x)=2ke˙gen​​L2(1−L2x2​)+Ts​

    Ts​=he˙gen​​L+T∞​

    Tmax​=2ke˙gen​​L2+Ts​

    Adiabatic boundary condition:

    T(x)=2ke˙gen​​L2(1−L2x2​)+Ts​

    Ts​=he˙gen​​L+T∞​

    Conduction in a Solid Cylinder

    Temperature distribution:

    T(r)=4ke˙gen​​ro​2(1−ro​2r2​)+Ts​

    Ts​=Tmax​−4ke˙gen​​ro​2

    #Steady Heat Conduction

    Conduction resistance:

    Q˙​cond​=L/kAT1​−T2​​=Rwall​T1​−T2​​

    Convection resistance:

    Q˙​conv​=1/hAs​Ts​−T∞​​=Rconv​Ts​−T∞​​

    Radiation resistance:

    Q˙​rad​=1/hrad​As​Ts​−Tsurr​​=Rrad​Ts​−Tsurr​​

    #Conduction in a Plane Wall

    Thermal resistance total heat transfer equation:

    Q˙​=Rtotal​T∞1​​−T∞2​​​=∑RΔT​=UA⋅ΔT

    where U is the overall heat transfer coefficient

    Multilayer plane wall:

    Q˙​=R i−j​Ti​−Tj​​

    where i−j follows the direction of steady heat transfer,
    and     Ri−j​ is the thermal resistance between locations i and j

    Thermal contact resistance:

    Rtc′′​=htc​1​=Q˙​/AΔTinterface​​

    Thermal contact conductance:

    htc​=ΔTinterface​Q˙​/A​

    #Conduction in a Hollow Cylinder and Sphere

    Total heat transfer for a hollow cylinder:

    Q˙​cond,cyl​=2πLk⋅ln(r2​/r1​)T1​−T2​​

    Rcyl​=2πLkln(r2​/r1​)​

    where r2​ is outer radius and r1​ is inner radius

    Total heat transfer for a hollow sphere:

    Q˙​cond,sph​=4πk(T1​−T2​)⋅r2​−r1​r1​r2​​

    Rsph​=4πr1​r2​kr2​−r1​​

    where r2​ is outer radius and r1​ is inner radius

    Multilayer plane cylinder or sphere:

    Q˙​=R i−j​Ti​−Tj​​

    where i−j follows the direction of steady heat transfer,
    and     Ri−j​ is the thermal resistance between locations i and j

    Critical radius of insulation:

    rcr,cyl​=hk​

    rcr,sph​=h2k​

    #Heat Transfer from Extended Surfaces (Fins)

    General heat transfer equation for a fin:

    0=dxd​(kAc​dxdT​)−hp(T−T∞​)

    Note that the equation includes both thermal conductivity
    of the fin and convection coefficient of the surrounding fluid.

    Fin with constant cross section and thermal conductivity,

    0=dx2d2T​−kAc​hp​(T−T∞​)

    0=dx2d2θ​−m2θ

    where excess temperature θ=T−T∞​ and m2=kAc​hp​

    General solutions to differential equation:

    θ(x)=C1​emx+C2​e−mx

    θ(x)=C1​cosh(mx)+C2​sinh(mx)

    Excess temperature definition (base of the fin):

    θ(0)=θb​=Tb​−T∞​

    #Boundary Conditions at Fin Tip

    Procedure for fin calculation:

    • If it is stated that the fin is infinite, or the fin tip has a specified temperature,
      or the fin has an adiabatic tip, use the respective equations for each scenario
    • If mL≥2.65 (for fin heat transfer) or mL≥4.6 (for fin
      heat transfer and fin temperature), use infinite fin equation
    • If the ratio Afin​Ac​​ is extremely small, use adiabatic fin equation
    • Else, use convective tip equation or approximate using Lc​

    Infinitely long fin, where Ttip​=T∞​:

    θb​θ​=Tb​−T∞​T−T∞​​=e−mx=e−xhp/kAc​​

    Q˙​fin​=hpkAc​​(Tb​−T∞​)

    Adiabatic fin tip, where Q˙​tip​=0:

    θb​θ​=Tb​−T∞​T−T∞​​=cosh mLcosh m(L−x)​

    Q˙​fin​=hpkAc​​(Tb​−T∞​)⋅tanh mL

    Specified temperature at fin tip, where Ttip​=TL​:

    θb​θ​=Tb​−T∞​T−T∞​​=sinh mL(θL​/θb​)sinh mx+sinh m(L−x)​

    Q˙​fin​=hpkAc​​(Tb​−T∞​)⋅sinh mLcosh mL−(θL​/θb​)​

    Convective heat loss at fin tip:

    θb​θ​=Tb​−T∞​T−T∞​​=cosh mL+(h/mk)sinh mLcosh m(L−x)+(h/mk)sinh m(L−x)​

    Q˙​fin​=hpkAc​​(Tb​−T∞​)⋅cosh mL+(h/mk)sinh mLsinh mL+(h/mk)cosh mL​

    #Fin Effectiveness

    If εfin​≥2, the addition of fins is beneficial.

    Effectiveness of a fin:

    εfin​=Q˙​no fin​Q˙​fin​​=hAb​(Tb​−T∞​)Q˙​fin​​

    εfin​=1 indicates that adding fins does not affect heat transfer at all.
    εfin​<1 indicates that the fin acts as insulation (reduce heat transfer).
    εfin​>1 indicates that the fin increases heat transfer from the surface.

    Effectiveness of an infinite fin with uniform cross-section:

    εlong fin​=hAb​(Tb​−T∞​)hpkAc​​(Tb​−T∞​)​=hAc​kp​​

    #Fin Efficiency

    Maximum heat transfer from a fin:

    Q˙​fin,max​=hAfin​(Tb​−T∞​)

    where Afin​ is total surface area of fin

    Fin efficiency:

    ηfin​=Q˙​fin,max​Q˙​fin​​=hAfin​(Tb​−T∞​)Q˙​fin​​

    Thermal resistance of a fin:

    Rfin​=Q˙​fin​Tb​−T∞​​=hAfin​ηfin​1​

    Efficiency of a fin with an adiabatic tip:

    ηadiab​=mLtanh mL​

    Corrected Fin Length

    Fin with convective heat loss at the tip:

    Lc​=L+pAc​​

    Rectangular cross-section fin:

    Lc,rect​=L+2t​

    Cylindrical cross-section fin:

    Lc,cyl​=L+4D​

    For a rectangular fin, if 2kht​<0.0625, use Lc,rect​.

    For a pin fin, if 2khD​<0.0625, use Lc,cyl​.

    Overall Efficiency (Multiple Fins)

    Overall surface efficiency:

    ηo​=Q˙​max​Q˙​tot​​=hAtot​(Tb​−T∞​)Q˙​tot​​

    where Atot​ is total exposed area
    of the fin and un-finned surfaces

    Alternative equation,

    Q˙​tot​=Q˙​fin​+Q˙​unfin​

    Q˙​tot​=ηfin​hAfin​θb​+hAb​θb​

    Q˙​tot​=hθb​(ηfin​Afin​+Ab​)

    Q˙​tot​=hθb​[ηfin​Afin​+(Atot​−Afin​)]

    Q˙​tot​=hAtot​θb​[1−Atot​Afin​​(1−ηfin​)]

    ηo​=1−Atot​Afin​​(1−ηfin​)

    Note that Afin​ is total surface area of the fins.

    #Transient Heat Conduction

    Lumped capacitance equation:

    θi​θ​=Ti​−T∞​T(t)−T∞​​=e−t/τ

    where time constant τ=hAs​ρVc​

    Biot number:

    Bi=Q˙​cond​Q˙​conv​​=kALΔT​hAΔT​=khL​

    Lumped capacitance model is valid if Bi<0.1.

    Characteristic length for an arbitrary shape:

    Lc​=As​V​

    Alternative lumped capacitance equation:

    θi​θ​=Ti​−T∞​T(t)−T∞​​=e−Bi⋅Fo

    where Fourier number Fo=Lc​2αt​

    Total heat transfer from a body to the environment:

    Q=ρVc(1−e−t/τ)

    Total heat transfer from the environment to a body:

    Q=−ρVc(1−e−t/τ)

    #Fundamentals of Convection

    Fluid in contact with a surface:

    q˙​conv​=q˙​cond​

    hx​(Ts​−T∞​)=−kf​∂y∂T​​y=0​

    hx​=Ts​−T∞​−kf​∂y∂T​​y=0​​

    Due to the no-slip condition, heat transfer from a solid’s surface
    to the fluid layer adjacent to the surface is by pure conduction.

    Reynolds number:

    Re=μρVL​=νVL​

    Nusselt number:

    Nu=kf​hLc​​

    Prandtl number:

    Pr=kμcp​​=αν​

    #Velocity Boundary Layer

    Shear stress of fluid in contact with surface:

    τs​=μ∂y∂u​​y=0​

    Local friction coefficient:

    Cf,x​=21​ρV2τs,x​​

    Average friction coefficient:

    Cˉf​=L1​∫0L​ Cf,x​ dx

    Total drag force on a surface:

    Ff​=τˉs​As​=21​ρV2As​Cˉf​

    #Differential Convection Equations

    Continuity equation:

    ∂x∂u​+∂y∂v​=0

    Simplified x-momentum equation:

    u∂x∂u​+v∂y∂u​=ν∂y2∂2u​−ρ1​∂x∂P​

    Inertia forces = Viscous + Pressure forces

    Note that for a flat plate, ∂x∂P​=0.

    Simplified y-momentum equation:

    ∂y∂P​=0

    Simplified energy equation:

    u∂x∂T​+v∂y∂T​=α∂y2∂2T​+cp​ν​(∂y∂u​)2

    Advection = Conduction + Viscous Dissipation

    #Laminar Flow over a Flat Plate

    Reynolds analogy:

    Cf,x​=ReL​2​Nux​

    Stx​=2Cf,x​​=ReL​PrNux​​=ρcp​Vhx​​

    Equations are only valid for when Pr=1.

    Chilton-Colburn analogy (modified Reynolds analogy):

    Cf,x​2ReL​​=Nux​Pr−1/3

    2Cf,x​​=Stx​Pr2/3=jH​

    Equations are only valid for 0.6<Pr<60.

    #External Forced Convection

    Fluid properties at evaluated at film temperature:

    Tfilm​=2Ts​+T∞​​

    Correction for ν if P∞​=Patm​:

    ν=P∞​Patm​​⋅ν1atm​

    Correction for kinematic viscosity is only required for gases.

    #Flow over Flat Plates

    Critical Reynolds number for a flat plate:

    Recr​=μρVxcr​​=5×105

    Reynolds number at which flow transitions from laminar to turbulent.

    Boundary layer thickness:

    δ=Rex​​4.91x​ (Laminar)

    δ=Rex​1/50.38x​ (Turbulent)

    Local friction coefficient:

    Cf,x​=Rex​​0.664​ (Laminar)

    Cf,x​=Rex​1/50.059​ (Turbulent)

    Average friction coefficient:

    Cˉf​=ReL​​1.33​ (Laminar)

    Cˉf​=ReL​1/50.074​ (Turbulent)

    Cˉf​=ReL​1/50.074​−ReL​1742​ (Laminar + Turbulent)

    Local Nusselt number:

    Nux​=0.332Rex​1/2Pr1/3 (Laminar + Pr>0.6)

    Nux​=0.0296Rex​4/5Pr1/3 (Turbulent + 0.6≤Pr≤60)

    Nux​=0.565(Rex​Pr)1/2=0.565Pex​1/2 (Liquid metals with high k)

    Average Nusselt number:

    Nuˉ=0.664ReL​1/2Pr1/3 (Laminar)

    Nuˉ=0.037ReL​4/5Pr1/3 (Turbulent)

    Nuˉ=(0.037ReL​4/5−871)Pr1/3 (Laminar + Turbulent)

    #Flow across Cylinders and Spheres

    Average Nusselt number (cylinder):

    Nuˉcyl​=khˉD​=0.3+[1+(0.4/Pr)2/3]1/40.62Re1/2Pr1/3​[1+(282000Re​)5/8]4/5

    Average Nusselt number (sphere):

    Nuˉsph​=khˉD​=2+[0.4Re1/2+0.06Re2/3]Pr2/5(μs​μ∞​​)1/4

    where fluid properties are evaluated at the freestream temperature and,

    3.5≤Re≤8×104, and 0.7≤Pr≤380, and 1.0≤μμ∞​​≤3.2

    Average Nusselt number (sphere):

    Nuˉsph​=2

    for Re≤0.5 and CD​=Re24​

    #Internal Forced Convection

    Average velocity of a flow:

    Vavg​=R22​∫0R​ r⋅u(r) dr

    where u(r) is the velocity profile

    Mean temperature of a flow:

    Tm​=Vavg​R22​∫0R​ r⋅T(r)u(r) dr

    where T(r) is the temperature profile

    Bulk mean fluid temperature of a flow:

    Tm,bulk​=2Inlet+Exit​=2Tm,i​+Tm,e​​

    #Entrance Region

    Entry region (laminar flow):

    x=0.05ReD​⋅D

    where ReD​<2300

    Thermal entry length (laminar flow):

    Lt,lami​=0.05ReD​PrD

    Entry region (turbulent flow):

    x>10D

    where ReD​>2300

    Thermal entry length (turbulent flow):

    Lt,turb​>10D

    Hydraulic Diameters

    Hydraulic diameter (non-circular tubes):

    Dh​=p4Ac​​

    where p is the wetted diameter

    Hydraulic diameter of an annulus:

    Dh​=Do​−Di​

    where Do​ is outer diameter and Di​ is inner diameter

    #General Thermal Analysis

    From 1st law of thermodynamics, heat transfer to a fluid:

    Q˙​=m˙cp​(Tm,e​−Tm,i​)

    Surface heat flux:

    q˙​s​=hx​(Ts​−Tm​)

    Constant Surface Heat Flux

    Surface heat flux:

    Q˙​=q˙​s​As​

    Q˙​=hAs​(Ts​−Tm​)

    Q˙​=m˙cp​(Tm,e​−Tm,i​)

    Mean fluid temperature at exit:

    Tm,e​=Tm,i​+m˙cp​q˙​s​As​​

    Tm​(x)=Tm,i​+m˙cp​q˙​s​p​x

    Surface temperature of exit:

    Ts,e​=Tm,e​+hq˙​s​​

    Relations between equations:

    ∂x∂T​=dxdTs​​=dxdTm​​=m˙cp​q˙​s​p​=m˙cp​h(Ts​−Tm​)πD​

    Constant Surface Temperature

    Mean fluid temperature at exit:

    lnTs​−Tm,i​Ts​−Tm,e​​=−m˙cp​hˉAs​​

    LMTD:

    ΔTlm​=ln(ΔTm,e​/ΔTm,i​)ΔTm,e​−ΔTm,i​​

    where ΔTm,e​=Ts,e​−Tm,e​
    and     ΔTm,i​=Ts,i​−Tm,i​

    Number of transfer units (NTU):

    NTU=m˙cp​hˉAs​​=m˙cp​hˉpx​

    #Average Nusselt Numbers

    Laminar Flow

    Fully developed flow (both velocity and temperature profiles are developed):

    Nu=4.36 (constant surface heat flux)

    Nu=3.66 (constant surface temperature)

    Fully developed velocity profile only (constant surface temperature):

    NuˉD​=3.66+1+0.04[(D/L)RePr]2/30.065(D/L)RePr​

    Not yet developed flow (constant surface temperature):

    NuˉD​=1.86(LRePrD​)1/3(μs​μbulk​​)0.14

    where 0.6≤Pr≤5 and 0.0044≤μs​μbulk​​≤9.75

    Turbulent Flow

    NuD​=0.023ReD​4/5Prn

    where ReD​≥10000, and 0.7≤Pr≤160, and DL​≥10

    For heating, where Ts​>Tm​ the exponent n=0.4.
    For cooling, where Ts​<Tm​ the exponent n=0.3.

    #Natural Convection

    Volume expansion coefficient:

    β=V1​(∂T∂V​)P​=−ρ1​(∂T∂ρ​)P​

    ρ∞​−ρs​=ρβ(Ts​−T∞​)

    For an ideal gas:

    β=Tfilm​1​

    where temperature is in Kelvins
    (only applicable to ideal gases)

    Grashof number:

    GrL​=ν2gβ(Ts​−T∞​)Lc​3​

    If ReL​2GrL​​≫1, natural convection effects dominate.

    If ReL​2GrL​​≪1, forced convection effects dominate.

    If ReL​2GrL​​=1, both effects must be considered.

    Rayleigh number:

    RaL​=ν2gβ(Ts​−T∞​)Lc​3Pr​=ναgβ(Ts​−T∞​)Lc​3​

    #Natural Convection over Surfaces

    Vertical Plate

    Laminar or turbulent flow:

    Nu lami​=0.59RaL​1/4 where 104<RaL​<109

    Nu turb​=0.1RaL​1/3 where 109<RaL​<1013

    Average Nusselt number for laminar flow:

    NuˉL​=0.68+[1+(0.492/Pr)9/16]4/90.67RaL​1/4​

    Average Nusselt number for entire range of Rayleigh number:

    NuˉL​={0.825+[1+(0.492/Pr)9/16]8/270.387RaL​1/6​}2

    Horizontal Plate

    Characteristic length:

    Lc​=PerimeterHeat Transfer Area​=pAs​​

    Nusselt numbers for upper surface of hot plate or lower surface of cold plate:

    NuˉL​=0.54RaL​1/4 where 104<RaL​<107

    NuˉL​=0.15RaL​1/5 where 107<RaL​<1011

    Nusselt numbers for lower surface of hot plate or upper surface of cold plate:

    NuˉL​=0.27RaL​1/4 where 105<RaL​<1011

    Vertical Cylinder

    Treated as a vertical plate if:

    D≥GrL​1/435L​

    where L is the height of the cylinder

    Horizontal Cylinder

    Average Nusselt number:

    NuˉD​={0.6+[1+(0.559/Pr)9/16]8/270.387RaD​1/6​}2

    where RaD​≤1012

    Sphere

    Average Nusselt number:

    NuˉD​=2+[1+(0.469/Pr)9/16]4/90.589RaD​1/4​

    where RaD​≤1011 and Pr≥0.7

    #Heat Exchangers

    #Overall Heat Transfer Coefficient

    Total thermal resistance:

    Rtot​=Rconv,i​+Rwall​+Rconv,o​

    UAs​1​=hi​Ai​1​+2πkLln(Do​/Di​)​+ho​Ao​1​

    Total thermal resistance with fouling:

    UAs​1​=hi​Ai​1​+Ai​Rf,i​​+2πkLln(Do​/Di​)​+Ao​Rf,o​​+ho​Ao​1​

    where Rf,i​ and Rf,o​ are the fouling factors of the inner and outer surfaces

    #Log Mean Temperature Difference

    Rate of heat transfer in exchanger:

    Q˙​=UAs​ΔTlm​

    Parallel-flow double-pipe: ΔT2​=Th,out​−Tc,out​ and ΔT1​=Th,in​−Tc,in​
    Counter-flow double-pipe:     ΔT2​=Th,out​−Tc,in​ and ΔT1​=Th,in​−Tc,out​
    Note that the above equation is only valid for double-pipe heat exchangers.

    Correction factor for cross-flow and shell-and-tube exchangers:

    ΔTlm​=F⋅ΔTlm,CF​

    Special cases where F=1:

    • Temperature of one fluid is constant (condensation/boiling)
    • Both fluids have the same heat capacity in a counter-flow double-pipe exchanger

    #Effectiveness — NTU

    Heat capacities of cold and hot fluid:

    Cc​=m˙c​cp,c​

    Ch​=m˙h​cp,h​

    where cp​ are the specific heat capacities

    Effectiveness of a heat exchanger:

    ε=Q˙​max​Q˙​actual​​=Cmin​(Th,in​−Tc,in​)Q˙​actual​​

    where Cmin​ is the smaller of Ch​ and Cc​

    Effectiveness of a parallel-flow double-pipe exchanger:

    εpara​=1+c1−exp[−NTU(1+c)]​

    where NTU=Cmin​UAs​​ and heat capacity ratio c=Cmax​Cmin​​

    #Radiation Heat Transfer

    Absorptivity:

    α=IncidentAbsorbed​=GGabs​​

    Reflectivity:

    ρ=IncidentReflected​=GGref​​

    Transmissivity:

    τ=IncidentTransmit​=GGtr​​

    where G is irradiation

    #View Factor

    Reciprocity relation:

    Ai​Fij​=Aj​Fji​

    Note that Fij​=Fji​ unless the areas of both surfaces are equal.

    Summation rule:

    j=1∑n​Fi→j​=F1→1​+F1→2​+⋯+F1→n​=1

    Note that the rule only applies to enclosures (enclosed surfaces).

    Superposition rule:

    Fi→j​=Fi→j1​+Fi→j2​+⋯+Fi→jn​

    Note that Fji​=Fj1→i​+Fj2→i​+⋯+Fjn→i​.

    Symmetry rule:

    Fij​=Fik​

    Two or more surfaces that possess symmetry about a common surface.

    #Radiation Exchange between Surfaces

    Radiosity of a surface:

    J=Eemit​+Gref​

    J=εEb​+ρG

    J=εEb​+(1−ε)G

    G=1−εJ−εEb​​

    For a gray, opaque surface, τ=0.

    1=α+ρ+τ

    ρ=1−α

    ρ=1−ε

    Net energy leaving a surface:

    AQ˙​​=J−G

    AQ˙​​=J−1−εJ−εEb​​

    AQ˙​​=1−εJ(1−ε)−(J−εEb​)​

    AQ˙​​=1−ε(Eb​−J)ε​

    Blackbody emissive power:

    Ebi​=σTi​4

    where Ti​ is temperature of the surface in Kelvins

    Surface Resistance to Radiation

    Q˙​i​=(1−εi​)/εi​Ai​Ebi​−Ji​​=Ri​Ebi​−Ji​​

    Ri​=ϵi​Ai​1−εi​​

    If Eb​>J, heat loss from the surface.
    If     Eb​<J, heat gain by the surface.

    For a blackbody, ε=1 and α=1,

    Ri​=0

    Ebi​=Ji​

    Space Resistance between 2 Surfaces

    Net radiation exchange between 2 surfaces:

    Q˙​i−j​=Ji​Ai​Fi−j​−Jj​Aj​Fj−i​

    Q˙​i−j​=Ji​Ai​Fi−j​−Jj​Ai​Fi−j​

    Q˙​i−j​=Ai​Fi−j​(Ji​−Jj​)

    Q˙​i−j​=1/(Ai​Fi−j​)Ji​−Jj​​

    Ri−j​=Ai​Fi−j​1​

    Resistance Network of Multiple Surfaces

    Network consists of:

    • Surface resistance of each surface
    • Space resistance between surfaces
    • Sum of heat transfer at each radiosity node is zero

    Node equations:

    R1​Eb1​−J1​​+R12​J2​−J1​​+R13​J3​−J1​​=0

    R2​Eb2​−J2​​+R12​J1​−J2​​+R23​J3​−J2​​=0

    R3​Eb3​−J3​​+R13​J1​−J3​​+R23​J2​−J3​​=0

    #Radiation Shielding

    Rate of heat transfer between infinite parallel plates with 1 radiation shield:

    Q˙​12, one shield​=ε1​A1​1−ε1​​+A1​F13​1​+ε3,1​A3​1−ε3,1​​+ε3,2​A3​1−ε3,2​​+A3​F32​1​+ε2​A2​1−ε2​​Eb1​−Eb2​​

    Rate of heat transfer between infinite parallel plates with N shields:

    Q˙​12, N shields​=(ε1​1​+ε2​1​−1)+(ε3,1​1​+ε3,2​1​−1)+ … +(εN,1​1​+εN,2​1​−1)Aσ(T1​4−T2​4)​

    If emissivities of all surfaces are equal, the above equation reduces to:

    Q˙​12, N shields​=N+11​ Q˙​12, no shields​=N+11​[ε1​+ε1​−1Aσ(T1​4−T2​4)​]
